description:
## Question

Which mechanism gives local cache hits (same daemon, restarts, `buck2 clean`, other checkouts) on darwin and Linux, while letting remote execution take over sharing later? Record the choice as an ADR under `docs/adr/`. The candidates as they stood at charting time:

- **(A) Native test execution caching through a local remote-execution service with workers.** The rule flag plus an executor that allows caching. Tests execute on localhost workers, so buck2 stores and serves them from the action cache.
- **(B) Tests as build actions.** The test runs as an ordinary `run` action that records its outcome in an output file. buck2 sees a trivial replay test. Results persist through a local cache-only server with `allow_cache_uploads`.
- **(C) A runner-owned cache.** A custom `v2_test_executor` computes its own key and reports recorded results without executing.
- **(D) Patch buck2** to cache and upload local test executions.

It must honour the reuse policy and cache-hit UX decided in the blocking tickets.
title: Which mechanism makes test results cacheable locally and remotely?
